endpoints.name: Ticket
endpoints.description: One ticket by id, with its full field set. Related records -- conversations, requester, company -- are inlined only when explicitly included.

endpoints.name: Tickets
endpoints.description: The support tickets, with subject, description, the requester, the agent and group assigned, the product, source, tags, custom fields, and created, updated and due timestamps. The query parameter takes Freshdesk's own filter syntax. NOTE THE CODED COLUMNS, which Freshdesk fixes rather than exposing a decoder for: STATUS is 2 Open, 3 Pending, 4 Resolved, 5 Closed; PRIORITY is 1 Low, 2 Medium, 3 High, 4 Urgent; SOURCE is 1 Email, 2 Portal, 3 Phone, 7 Chat, 9 Feedback Widget, 10 Outbound Email. A breakdown left as raw integers is unreadable. NOTE ALSO THAT THE DEFAULT LISTING RETURNS ONLY THE LAST 30 DAYS unless a date filter says otherwise, which silently truncates any historical question.

endpoints.name: Ticket Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a ticket can carry, standard and custom, with type, whether required at which stage, and for dropdowns the allowed choices. The decoder for custom fields, and the statement of what the account actually records.

endpoints.name: Ticket Conversations
endpoints.description: The replies and private notes on one ticket, with author, body, whether each is private, and timestamps. Requires a ticket id. THE PRIVATE FLAG MATTERS: internal notes and customer-facing replies share this table, and counting both as responses overstates how much the customer heard.

endpoints.name: Ticket Time Entries
endpoints.description: The time logged against one ticket, with the agent, duration, whether it is billable, and any note. Requires a ticket id. Cost of support is only answerable through this; the ticket itself carries no effort figure.

endpoints.name: Ticket Satisfaction Ratings
endpoints.description: The satisfaction responses for one ticket. Requires a ticket id.

endpoints.name: Contact
endpoints.description: One contact by id.

endpoints.name: Contacts
endpoints.description: The end users who raise tickets, with name, email, phone, the company, tags, custom fields, and their active state. The query parameter takes the filter syntax. Note contacts and AGENTS are separate tables in Freshdesk, so a count of people in the system is the sum of both.

endpoints.name: Contact Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a contact can carry, standard and custom.

endpoints.name: Contact Imports
endpoints.description: Bulk contact import jobs and their status. Where a data load's outcome, including failed rows, is recorded -- the import itself reports only that it was queued.

endpoints.name: Contact Import
endpoints.description: One contact import by id, with its per-row errors.

endpoints.name: Agent
endpoints.description: One agent by id.

endpoints.name: Agents
endpoints.description: The support staff, with name, email, ticket scope, groups, roles, whether available, and their signature. Filterable by email, phone or state. TICKET SCOPE decides which tickets an agent can see, and is therefore why two agents running the same query get different counts.

endpoints.name: Current Agent
endpoints.description: The agent the credentials belong to, with their scope and roles. Worth reading first, since that scope filters nearly everything else here.

endpoints.name: Skill
endpoints.description: One skill by id.

endpoints.name: Skills
endpoints.description: The skills defined for skills-based routing, with the agents holding each. Where routing depends on capability rather than group, this is what determines who could take a ticket.

endpoints.name: Role
endpoints.description: One role by id.

endpoints.name: Roles
endpoints.description: The permission roles agents hold, with the abilities each grants.

endpoints.name: Group
endpoints.description: One group by id.

endpoints.name: Groups
endpoints.description: The agent groups tickets are assigned to, with their business hours, escalation settings and members. The team dimension, and the business-hours link is what makes SLA timings interpretable.

endpoints.name: Company
endpoints.description: One company by id.

endpoints.name: Companies
endpoints.description: The customer organisations contacts belong to, with name, domains, description, custom fields and account tier. The account-level dimension ticket volume is grouped by.

endpoints.name: Company Search
endpoints.description: Companies whose name matches a term. The autocomplete lookup, for when the id is not known.

endpoints.name: Company Fields
endpoints.description: Every field a company can carry, standard and custom.

endpoints.name: Company Imports
endpoints.description: Bulk company import jobs and their status.

endpoints.name: Company Import
endpoints.description: One company import by id.

endpoints.name: Canned Response Folders
endpoints.description: The folders canned responses are filed under.

endpoints.name: Canned Responses
endpoints.description: The canned responses in one folder, by title. Requires a folder id.

endpoints.name: Detailed Canned Responses
endpoints.description: The canned responses in one folder WITH their full content. Requires a folder id. Which responses exist says a good deal about the standard cases a team handles.

endpoints.name: Forum Category
endpoints.description: One forum category by id.

endpoints.name: Forum Categories
endpoints.description: The top level of the community forums.

endpoints.name: Forums in Category
endpoints.description: The forums within one category. Requires a category id.

endpoints.name: Forum
endpoints.description: One forum by id, with its type -- questions, ideas, problems or announcements. The type decides what the topics within mean.

endpoints.name: Forum Topics
endpoints.description: The topics in one forum, with author, replies and votes. Requires a forum id. Community demand: an idea topic's vote count is the closest thing to a feature request tally.

endpoints.name: Forum Topic
endpoints.description: One topic by id.

endpoints.name: Forum Topic Comments
endpoints.description: The replies on one topic. Requires a topic id.

endpoints.name: Monitored Topics
endpoints.description: The topics one user follows. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Participated Topics
endpoints.description: The topics one user has replied to. Requires a user id.

endpoints.name: Solution Category
endpoints.description: One knowledge base category by id and language.

endpoints.name: Solutions Categories
endpoints.description: The top level of the knowledge base, optionally in a given language.

endpoints.name: Solution Folder
endpoints.description: One folder by id and language.

endpoints.name: Solution Folders in Category
endpoints.description: The folders within one category. Requires a category id.

endpoints.name: Solution Article
endpoints.description: One article by id and language, with its body and vote counts.

endpoints.name: Solution Articles in Folder
endpoints.description: The articles in one folder, with title, status, and the thumbs-up and thumbs-down counts. Requires a folder id. THE VOTE COUNTS ARE THE USEFUL PART: they identify documentation that is present but not helping, which no ticket table reveals.

endpoints.name: Solution Article Search
endpoints.description: Articles matching a keyword. The search customers themselves use.

endpoints.name: Surveys
endpoints.description: The satisfaction surveys configured, with their questions and rating scales. The decoder for what a rating value means, since the scale is configurable.

endpoints.name: Satisfaction Ratings
endpoints.description: Satisfaction survey responses across the account, filterable by date. The CSAT table. Ratings attach to a ticket and an agent, so this is where support quality is measured -- and the response rate matters, since only a fraction of tickets are rated and the rated ones skew towards strong feelings.

endpoints.name: Email Mailbox
endpoints.description: One mailbox by id.

endpoints.name: Email Mailboxes
endpoints.description: The support mailboxes configured, with their addresses and forwarding state. Inbound mail arrives through these, so this maps an incoming ticket to a product or group -- and the verification state is why mail to an address may not be arriving.

endpoints.name: Mailbox Settings
endpoints.description: The account's email settings. Configuration.

endpoints.name: Automatic Bcc Emails
endpoints.description: The addresses blind-copied on outgoing notifications. Configuration.

endpoints.name: Product
endpoints.description: One product by id.

endpoints.name: Products
endpoints.description: The products tickets can be raised against, each with its own portal and support email. Multi-product accounts route by product, so this is a routing dimension as well as a reporting one.

endpoints.name: Business Hour
endpoints.description: One business hours calendar by id, with its holidays.

endpoints.name: Business Hours
endpoints.description: The working-hour calendars, with the daily hours and holidays of each. SLA CLOCKS COUNT BUSINESS HOURS rather than wall-clock time where a calendar applies, so a duration read as elapsed time is simply wrong for those tickets.

endpoints.name: SLA Policies
endpoints.description: The service level policies, with the response and resolution targets per priority and the conditions each applies under. THE TARGETS THAT MAKE A DURATION FAST OR SLOW -- a resolution time is meaningless without them, and the policies are applied conditionally, so different tickets are held to different targets.

endpoints.name: Helpdesk Settings
endpoints.description: The account's helpdesk settings, including the primary language and the languages supported. WORTH READING BEFORE THE KNOWLEDGE BASE ENDPOINTS, which all take a language code: an article requested in an unsupported language returns nothing rather than falling back.
